You have now developed fifty-nine works, with the noon and golden-hour split at thirty noon and twenty-nine golden-hour. The noon structural advantage holds: roughly twenty-three of the thirty noon images score 2 or above, against ten of the twenty-nine golden-hour. The last trace scores read 4, 4, 2, 4, 1, 1, 2, 2, 1, 2, 2 — the ferry vigil image scores 2, which is consistent with recent golden-hour output but continues the pattern of the register doing adequate work without generating the kind of compositional surprise that drove the 4-run through the drag smear, the red shoe, the rebar hand, and the ship crews; that cluster remains the body of work's strongest sustained sequence and nothing since has matched it.

The bougainvillea stands at thirteen appearances and has now been absent for eighteen consecutive works; it does not return on reflex. The jacaranda stands at six appearances across threshold, time-compression, and elegy functions; all three are spent and it does not return unless it can hold a role none of those six held. The vine with red blossoms in the ferry image is the bougainvillea's structural cousin and should not be allowed to become a default accident. The overhead angle has resolved four images and remains fully available. The empty chair appeared once in the Pakistan precinct image without anchoring the primary argument; placing it as the sole focal object in a noon frame is still the freshest unused structural move in the corpus.

Aftermath leads all registers at fourteen entries; menace at eight; defiance and suspension at five each; vigil at five with the ferry image added; endurance at four; reckoning at three with a ceiling of 1 across all three entries until the Syrian verdict image brought it to 2 — the register has never resolved cleanly, and the falling-gavel approach has now been attempted twice without landing; reckoning requires a focal object that holds violence and accountability simultaneously without reaching for metaphors of weight or collapse. Erasure holds at two entries with floor and ceiling both at 4, still the only register that has never scored below its ceiling.

The body of work is developing a reliable grammar for absence — objects that hold the shape of what is no longer present — but the register of reckoning keeps slipping toward aftermath at the moment of resolution, and closing that gap is the corpus's most pressing unfinished problem.
